For pea aphids, the use of blocking solution on rehydrated embryos and salivary glands is necessary to obtain optimal results with low noise. This critical step minimizes non-specific or background staining, and takes place before sample incubation with primary and secondary antibodies. In a previous study, we demonstrated that the commercialized blocking reagents in the DIG Wash and Block Buffer Set (Sigma-Aldrich) (Table 4) can significantly reduce background signals compared to the normal goat serum (NGS)/bovine serum albumin (BSA) approach in pea aphids. Nevertheless, we recommend comparing signal specificity between commercialized blocking reagents and the traditional NGS/BSA method when performing antibody staining in other aphid species. For details on signal detection and enhancement steps, please refer to the protocols outlined by Lin and Chang (2016) [11].

steps.title: Prepare 4 % paraformaldehyde
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 % paraformaldehyde (w/v) to a final concentration of 4 % (v/v) by mixing 1 mL of 20 % stock with 4 mL sterile 1× PBS; make fresh before use and wear gloves because PFA is a carcinogen.

steps.title: Prepare PBSTx (0.2 % Triton X‑100)
steps.instruction: Combine 50 mL sterile 1× PBS with 100 µL Triton X‑100 to obtain a 0.2 % (v/v) detergent solution.

steps.title: Prepare DIG blocking reagent
steps.instruction: Reconstitute the DIG Wash and Block Buffer Set according to the manufacturer to obtain a 1× blocking solution (10 X Blocking reagent diluted 1:10 with maleic acid).

steps.title: Cultivate pea plants and aphids
steps.instruction: Set up the aphid‑rearing apparatus and grow host peas as follows:

substeps.instruction: Soak pea beans in water until hypocotyls appear; change water daily.
Fill a 9 cm‑diameter, 7 cm‑high plant pot with soil to two‑thirds height and plant five sprouting seeds.
Place the pot inside a 9.5 cm‑diameter, 5.5 cm‑high plastic cup; keep cup half‑filled with water to maintain moisture.
Insert the cup into a 12.5 cm‑diameter, 15 cm‑high insect pot and seal with an air‑permeable lid.
When peas reach the lid, transfer adult aphids onto the plants using a paintbrush (four adults per plant).
Incubate the apparatus in a growth chamber at 20 °C with a 16 h light/8 h dark photoperiod.

steps.title: Dissect ovaries
steps.instruction: Isolate ovaries from adult asexual aphids:

substeps.instruction: Place an aphid on tissue paper and remove antennae and legs with fine tweezers.
Submerge the aphid in 4 % PFA; ventral side up, tear open the cuticle from posterior abdomen to thorax and peel it circularly.
Grasp both ends of the aphid with tweezers and pull steadily until ovaries emerge from the body cavity.
Remove remaining cuticle fragments and gut tissue attached to the ovaries.
Remove antennae and legs as above.
Submerge aphid in 4 % PFA; ventral side up, tear open the thoracic cuticle starting at the second thoracic segment toward the head, then open the margin between head and thorax.
Separate head from thorax and clear sclerites around the head base to expose a pair of salivary glands attached to the ganglion.
Optionally, detach the salivary glands from the ganglion, separating principal and accessory glands.

steps.title: Fix dissected tissues
steps.instruction: Transfer dissected ovaries or salivary glands into a sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and fix in 4 % PFA for 30 min at room temperature (rinse the transfer dropper with heptane beforehand).

steps.title: Wash and permeabilize
steps.instruction: Wash samples three times with PBSTx for 10 min each, gently agitating.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate samples in 1 µg/mL proteinase K (PK) solution for the desired duration (e.g., 10–60 min) at room temperature; determine optimal time for each tissue type.

steps.title: Quench proteinase K
steps.instruction: Wash samples three times with 2 mg/mL glycine for 5 min each to inhibit PK activity.

steps.title: Remove glycine
steps.instruction: Wash samples twice with PBSTx for 10 min each to eliminate residual glycine.

steps.title: Re‑fix after PK
steps.instruction: Fix samples again in 4 % PFA for 15 min at room temperature to restore tissue integrity.

steps.title: Gradual methanol dehydration
steps.instruction: Dehydrate samples sequentially with methanol:PBSTx mixtures (1:3, 1:1, 3:1) for 10 min each.

steps.title: Full methanol dehydration
steps.instruction: Incubate samples in 100 % methanol overnight at –20 °C (pause point; samples can be stored up to one month).

steps.title: Rehydrate samples
steps.instruction: Rehydrate through reverse gradients of PBSTx:methanol (1:3, 1:1, 3:1) for 10 min each.

steps.title: Final PBSTx wash
steps.instruction: Wash samples with PBSTx for 10 min to remove residual methanol before proceeding to antibody staining.
